Our Final U-Pick Adventure of the Year at Daniel’s U-Pick
Windsor forks, Nova Scotia, Canada
body:
A last-minute plan often turns into one of the most memorable adventures. That was certainly true when our group recently visited Daniel’s U-Pick for our final fruit-and-vegetable-picking trip of the year.

We organized the trip only one day in advance. Altogether, our group included 10 people, including two children. We left the city at approximately 1:00 p.m. and arrived at the farm around 2:30 p.m. The farm is about 70-80 kilometres from the city, making it a convenient destination for a half-day getaway.

A Busy and Welcoming Farm

By the time we arrived, more than 50 vehicles were already parked at the farm. A wedding reception was also taking place nearby, making the entire area feel especially lively.

It was wonderful to see so many families and groups spending time outdoors and picking fresh produce. The farm is quite large, with plenty of space to walk around and explore.

We had visited Daniel’s U-Pick the previous year, but there had not been much produce available to pick at that time. This year was completely different. The garden was full of colourful fruits and vegetables, giving us many options to choose from.

Fresh Produce Straight from the Garden

During our visit, we picked berries, apples, pears, pumpkins, squash and several other seasonal items. There is something genuinely satisfying about choosing produce directly from the plants and bringing it home fresh from the farm.

The farm also sells homemade apple cider, which we tried and really enjoyed. We had hoped to purchase fresh farm eggs as well, but unfortunately, they were already sold out—and would remain unavailable for the next few days.

A Childhood Memory Brought Back to Life

One of the most enjoyable parts of the trip was seeing the farm’s free-range chickens. Although they were not for sale, visitors could watch and interact with them.

The two children in our group had a wonderful time playing nearby and feeding the chickens. For the adults, the experience brought back many childhood memories. Back home in Bangladesh, some of us grew up raising chickens around our houses, so seeing them roaming freely again after such a long time felt both exciting and nostalgic.

Sometimes, a simple moment can reconnect us with a part of our past that we had almost forgotten.

Is Daniel’s U-Pick Worth Visiting?

Overall, everyone in our group thoroughly enjoyed the trip. Daniel’s U-Pick is a good option for anyone who wants to experience farm life, spend time in nature and collect fresh seasonal produce.

Parking is convenient because spaces are available close to the garden. Although the farm is approximately 120 kilometres from the city, the journey is manageable and does not require an entire day. It can easily be enjoyed as a relaxed half-day trip with friends, family or children.

There are a few things visitors should know before going. A five-pound bag for apples or pears costs approximately $10, while a container for berries costs around $19. We found the prices slightly expensive, and the grapes we tasted were quite sour. Produce availability can also change quickly, so visitors looking for a particular item—especially fresh eggs—may want to contact the farm before travelling.

Despite those small drawbacks, it was a fun and memorable outing. We returned home with fresh produce, happy children, nostalgic memories and plenty of photographs from a beautiful day together.

For anyone looking for a quick and enjoyable countryside experience, Daniel’s U-Pick is certainly worth considering.

Please note: Prices and produce availability may vary depending on the season and the date of your visit.
title: Pick up fresh fruit and vegetables at Daniels u-pick
